For the night shift handover, please note the following:

Berth 3B remains occupied by MT Blue Nile until 0200 hrs tomorrow. She is discharging 18,000 tonnes of crude palm oil, and the shore gang reports a rate of 420 tonnes per hour. At that rate, completion is on schedule, but the hose connection at manifold No. 2 was swapped out at 16:10 due to a perished gasket. The replacement is rated for the same 150 mm service, so no change to the discharge plan. The terminal has asked that the vessel's agent be reminded about the slop disposal request submitted earlier – we have not received the signed copy.

Berth 7: Star Horizon is confirmed for 0600 hrs, pilot boarding at 0530 hrs. The mooring boat MV Ibom Power has been reserved and will standby at the eastern mole from 0515 hrs. Linesmen will be eight, plus one supervisor. The bollard spacing on Berth 7 is 24 metres, and the vessel's mooring arrangement is six headlines, four stern lines, two spring lines forward and two aft – that matches what we have on the plan. I have asked the linesmen to bring extra rat guards because the last few vessels have reported missing ones.

One issue: the fender at Berth 7, unit F-3, is showing wear.
